questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'Skills and knowledge of employees of course, will change because now you are using a very sophisticated software, and all employees will have to become computer savvy... he has to retrained and reskilled.'

questions.question: What is at the core of how an organization uses ERP, connecting all major functionalities?
options: A distributed ledger system
A central database
Individual departmental spreadsheets
External cloud storage.
questions.answer: A central database
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'How the organization uses ERP? - You have the central database and then you have the major functionalities on the all the four sides...'

questions.question: Which of the following is a functionality typically found in the Sales and Marketing area of ERP?
options: Quality assurance
Vendor rating
Pricing and rebates
Plant maintenance
questions.answer: Pricing and rebates
questions.explanation: The lecture lists for Sales and Marketing: 'pricing and rebates, sales planning, delivery dates, sales returns.'

questions.question: What is a major area within the Manufacturing module of ERP, as mentioned in the lecture?
options: Accounts receivable
Customer credit
Production planning
Cash in hand
questions.answer: Production planning
questions.explanation: The lecture lists for Manufacturing: 'production, planning, quality assurance, order fulfilment etc.'

questions.question: Besides inventory management, what other functionality is mentioned for the Purchasing and Materials module?
options: Sales planning
Customer credit
Vendor rating
Cash forecast
questions.answer: Vendor rating
questions.explanation: The lecture lists for Purchasing and Materials: 'Pending delivery, open Purchase orders, Vendor rating, Invoice verification, exports and imports etcetera.'

questions.question: In the Order Invoicing Process example, what program is run when there is a new order or change in a sales order to determine material needs?
options: Accounts Receivable Program
Materials Requirement Planning (MRP) program
Sales and Distribution Program
Quality Assurance Program
questions.answer: Materials Requirement Planning (MRP) program
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'Whenever, there is a new order or change in the sales order you run the MRP program (transaction).'

questions.question: Before creating a Purchase Order for items like batteries, what document does the MRP program first create?
options: Sales Order
Purchase Requisition
Invoice
Delivery Note
questions.answer: Purchase Requisition
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'But, first it will create a Purchase Requisition which the planner will convert to a Purchase Order...'

questions.question: The credit check performed by the sales manager is part of which ERP module?
options: Sales and Distribution (SD)
Materials Management (MM)
Finance (FI)
Production Planning (PP)
questions.answer: Finance (FI)
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'She goes and does a Credit Check in the Credit Management area which is a finance function (FI module).'

questions.question: When checking for goods in transit from a factory to a warehouse, which module's feature is being used?
options: Sales and Distribution (SD)
Warehouse Management (WM)
Production Planning (PP)
Finance (FI)
questions.answer: Warehouse Management (WM)
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'The feature being used is a part of warehouse management module (WM) which gives information about anything being shipped from Haldia to their warehouse in Mughal Sarai...'

questions.question: Upon completion of a quality inspection and acceptance of material, which accounts get updated?
options: Sales revenue and customer credit
Stock and consumption accounts
Cash in hand and accounts payable
Production planning and order fulfillment.
questions.answer: Stock and consumption accounts
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'On completion of inspection the stock and consumption accounts get updated. This is the accounting activity which happens as soon as the material gets accepted by the quality control.'

questions.question: What factors are used to rate vendors (A, B, or C) based on their performance after a goods receipt and quality inspection?
options: Timeliness of delivery and quality of product
Vendor's marketing strategy and brand recognition
Number of employees and company size
Geographic location and transport costs.
questions.answer: Timeliness of delivery and quality of product
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'If he had delivered on right time and 100 percent material got accepted , vendor gets an A rating. Otherwise he would have got say B rating because he delivered one day late. He may have delivered on time, but then 10 percent of the item got rejected. So, quality was a problem.'

questions.question: How does ERP contribute to revenue generation?
options: By reducing the number of product offerings
By limiting access to new market segments
Through increased asset utilization and broader product offering
By decreasing customer service interactions.
questions.answer: Through increased asset utilization and broader product offering
questions.explanation: The lecture lists 'Revenue generation through its ability to service new market segments, increased asset utilization and capacity through better planning, redeploying workforce into higher value added roles and broader product offering.'

questions.question: What is a key aspect of 'Better supplier management' facilitated by ERP, especially for multinational companies?
options: Decentralized purchasing with individual factory negotiations
Global centralized purchasing using strategic sourcing
Eliminating the need for vendor ratings
Reducing the number of suppliers to a single source.
questions.answer: Global centralized purchasing using strategic sourcing
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'Better supplier management - Global centralized purchasing using strategic sourcing with leveraged procurement spend.'

questions.question: To get the 'real right perspective' of an ERP system, from which angle should one primarily think?
options: The IT angle
The financial accounting angle
The business perspective
The technical programming angle
questions.answer: The business perspective
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'So, if you want to get the real right perspective of a ERP system or ERP software, think from the business perspective.'

questions.question: What two characteristics are repeatedly mentioned about ERP/SAP implementation?
options: Inexpensive and easy
Expensive and difficult
Quick and simple
Optional and minor
questions.answer: Expensive and difficult
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'because it is expensive. It is also expensive and difficult to implement SAP and not very easy.'

questions.question: Why do jobs and rewards change after ERP implementation?
options: Because the company wants to reduce overall salaries
Because roles and skill sets change, requiring retraining
Because ERP automates all jobs
Because employees resist new technology.
questions.answer: Because roles and skill sets change, requiring retraining
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'Jobs and rewards for example, will change because your roles will change and your skill sets will change. Jobs and rewards also need to change because the way a person was doing work previously before ERP and the way he will be doing after ERP implementation, will be it in a different way because the processes have changed and he will be working fully on IT system.'

questions.question: How does ERP impact company culture?
options: It makes the company less transparent
It has direct impact due to increased transparency, online, and real-time operations
It forces a more hierarchical culture
It eliminates the need for cultural norms.
questions.answer: It has direct impact due to increased transparency, online, and real-time operations
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'Company Structure and Culture gets impacted very much because now things are very transparent, online and real time and these have got direct impact on the culture of a company.'

questions.question: Besides the four major functions, which of the following is mentioned as another area where ERP is involved?
options: Legal department
Research and Development
Quality Management
Public Relations
questions.answer: Quality Management
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'other areas are also very much involved like - HR, Quality Management, Plant Maintenance, Service Management, Warehouse Management etc.'

questions.question: In the sales order enquiry example, what is the sales manager's response when the dealer emphasizes urgency but has an outstanding payment?
options: She immediately processes the urgent order
She tells him to clear the outstanding payment first
She transfers the call to the finance department
She offers a discount for immediate payment.
questions.answer: She tells him to clear the outstanding payment first
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'But if it is no and he has not paid up then she will tell him that against your past order of Rs.50 lakhs, Rs.10 lakhs is pending. Please release the cheque and I will process your new order.'

questions.question: What happens to the data elements (like date of supply, quantity approved by quality) generated by ERP transactions?
options: They are stored but not used for further analysis
They are used to generate information like vendor evaluation scores
They are manually compiled into reports
They are only accessible to the IT department.
questions.answer: They are used to generate information like vendor evaluation scores
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'The data elements are date of supply, quantity of items which got approved by quality etc. From this data, what information is generated? Information generated are vendor’s evaluation score.'

questions.question: How does ERP generally affect decision-making within an organization?
options: It makes decision-making more complicated due to too much data
It centralizes all decisions to a single point
It makes decision-making less complicated with reduced hierarchical levels
It requires external consultants for every decision.
questions.answer: It makes decision-making less complicated with reduced hierarchical levels
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'However, with ERP, once you break down the walls, and restructure the organization, it makes decision making less complicated with reduced hierarchical levels.'

questions.question: The lecture repeatedly emphasizes the importance of information in ERP. What is the core idea behind this emphasis?
options: Information is power, enabling quick and informed decisions
Information is primarily for auditing purposes
Information is only useful for IT specialists
Information slows down business processes.
questions.answer: Information is power, enabling quick and informed decisions
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'So, when you have information you have power... That is the power of ERP, the power of SAP and that is what managing information system is all about.'

questions.question: The lecture concludes that all business processes, regardless of their starting point, eventually end in which department?
options: Sales and Marketing
Production
Finance
Human Resources
questions.answer: Finance
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'See finally, everything has to end in the finance because end of the day you know it’s all about my account getting credited with money. So, that is how the whole business works everywhere. So, all process will end somehow in finance.'

questions.question: According to the lecture, what is the typical minimum duration for an ERP implementation project in a large organization?
options: A) 1 month
B) 3 months
C) 6 months
D) 1 year
questions.answer: C) 6 months
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'it could take from at least 6 months to sometimes couple of years.'

questions.question: What is the term commonly used to refer to an ERP implementation where no changes are made to the software product from a technical perspective, sticking to what the product offers?
options: A) Custom implementation
B) Vanilla implementation
C) Hybrid implementation
D) Agile implementation
questions.answer: B) Vanilla implementation
questions.explanation: The lecture mentions, 'This is commonly referred as a vanilla implementation where no change is being done to the software product from a technical perspective.'

questions.question: During which phase of an ERP implementation project are stakeholders like the CFO, CMO, and head of production required to agree and sign off on the 'To-Be' processes proposed by the product?
options: A) Project Preparation Phase
B) Realization Phase
C) Business Blueprint Phase
D) Final Preparation Phase
questions.answer: C) Business Blueprint Phase
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'Business blueprint is a design phase, when you are actually designing the To-Be process... So, all your stakeholders from the company side like the CFO, the chief of Marketing... everybody will have to agree to the new processes... And they will have to sign off 'yes', we agree and once that whole thing is signed off, then you move into the Realization Phase.'

questions.question: Which of the following is identified as a 'very big risk' for an ERP project, emphasizing the need for management's backing?
options: A) Computer literacy of employees
B) Connectivity in remote locations
C) Lack of top management support
D) Aggressive time frame
questions.answer: C) Lack of top management support
questions.explanation: The lecture lists 'Lack of top management support, its it is a very big risk; the management has to support your project.'

questions.question: What is the primary activity associated with the 'Sustain' phase of an ERP project?
options: A) Designing the 'To-Be' processes
B) Training end-users
C) Maintenance and upgrades
D) Initial risk analysis
questions.answer: C) Maintenance and upgrades
questions.explanation: The lecture describes the Sustain phase as 'maintenance because any software you know has to be continuously maintained and upgraded.'

questions.question: If an organization decides to retain its existing payroll software and connect it with the new SAP system, what type of scope is primarily being addressed?
options: A) Technical enhancement scope
B) Organizational scope
C) Interface scope
D) Data conversion scope
questions.answer: C) Interface scope
questions.explanation: The lecture explains, 'Interface scope - is the scope that is how many of the existing software, you want to retain and build a bridge, that is, custom software to connect these softwares with SAP software... like I said the payroll. If you want to use existing payroll system, fine you can use it; but then, you have to build a connecting program and we call it an interface.'

questions.question: During the Business Blueprint phase, if a company's unique process is not covered by the standard SAP product, what is this situation referred to, and what is the recommended approach to address it?
options: A) It's called a 'feature request,' and it should always be implemented.
B) It's called a 'gap,' and custom development should be minimized.
C) It's called a 'deviation,' and it requires immediate re-engineering.
D) It's called an 'enhancement,' and it's always a best practice.
questions.answer: B) It's called a 'gap,' and custom development should be minimized.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'This is called Fit-Gap in the sense after the design you can realize that some of the process of this company are very unique. They are not covered in the SAP product. So, that is called we call this as a gap... So, the custom development should be kept to the minimum to reduce cost and a high system performance.'

questions.question: What is identified as the 'most important starting activity' in the Project Preparation phase?
options: A) System performance testing
B) Training of team members
C) Go-Live planning
D) Data conversion
questions.answer: B) Training of team members
questions.explanation: The lecture says, 'Training is the most important starting activity in this phase, where you have to train the client’s team members in SAP software...'

questions.question: In the Realization phase of an SAP project, what is the primary method used by functional resources to adapt the software to business needs, without writing new code?
options: A) Programming
B) Customization (Configuration)
C) Interface development
D) Data migration
questions.answer: B) Customization (Configuration)
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'Now, in SAP is something is known as Customization. Here you do not need actually programmers or coders to customize the software because it is already prebuilt... they will now configure the product by writing some formula, selecting some check boxes, putting some values etcetera...'

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT explicitly listed as a project implementation challenge in the lecture?
options: A) Unrealistic Expectations
B) Process Redesign Challenges
C) Complex Interfaces
D) Lack of hardware availability
questions.answer: D) Lack of hardware availability
questions.explanation: The lecture lists 'Scope change; Budget change, Long timelines... Process Redesign Challenges, Unrealistic Expectations and Complex Interfaces' as challenges. While hardware is part of technical infrastructure, 'lack of hardware availability' is not explicitly listed as a project implementation challenge in the same section as the others.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of 'Data Conversion' in an ERP project?
options: A) To design new reports and forms.
B) To transfer existing data from legacy systems into the new ERP system in a compatible format.
C) To build interfaces between SAP and other software.
D) To train users on new data entry methods.
questions.answer: B) To transfer existing data from legacy systems into the new ERP system in a compatible format.
questions.explanation: The lecture explains, 'Data conversion scope - Original data which are there in the legacy system from the existing softwares will have to be now transported into SAP. So, that is called data conversion. Conversion, because it has to be converted into a format which you are designing for the new product.'

questions.question: Why might an organization need to develop custom reports and forms in an SAP implementation, even if SAP offers standard ones?
options: A) To reduce the overall project cost.
B) To ensure future maintenance is easier.
C) To replicate existing templates and formats familiar to management, and include statutory information.
D) To avoid any technical enhancements.
questions.answer: C) To replicate existing templates and formats familiar to management, and include statutory information.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'Normally, SAP, they have their own standard reports which are good enough, but sometimes you want to have reports in your existing template and formats which your management team ( specially Senior Management ) is used to working with... Similarly, for forms... your company logo will be there, company address will be there, company PAN number will be there... So, many important statutory information has to be there in these forms.'

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as one of the four key dimensions required as part of the ERP implementation journey?
options: A) People
B) Process
C) Budget
D) Technology
questions.answer: C) Budget
questions.explanation: The lecture lists the dimensions as 'People, Process, Knowledge and Technology.'

questions.question: What is the primary reason given for minimizing technical enhancements or custom development in an ERP project?
options: A) To increase the project's duration.
B) To introduce more bugs and increase maintenance issues.
C) To reduce cost, improve system performance, and minimize future maintenance issues.
D) To make the software heavier and impact response time.
questions.answer: C) To reduce cost, improve system performance, and minimize future maintenance issues.
questions.explanation: The lecture advises, 'you should try to minimize the technical enhancements... because from a future maintenance perspective, the less the amount of code you write better it is for the software quality because the more you write codes, you can actually produce lot of bugs... So, the custom development should be kept to the minimum to reduce cost and a high system performance.'

questions.question: What signifies the 'Go-Live' day in an ERP implementation?
options: A) The day the project preparation begins.
B) The day the old systems are shut down and the new SAP software is used for business operations.
C) The day user training is completed.
D) The day the business blueprint is signed off.
questions.answer: B) The day the old systems are shut down and the new SAP software is used for business operations.
questions.explanation: The lecture defines Go-Live as 'the day you shut down your old systems and start working and carrying out your business with the new SAP software.'

questions.question: In the five-step project risk management approach, what action immediately follows estimating the probability of occurrence for a potential risk?
options: A) Finding the potential risk element.
B) Doing an impact analysis.
C) Prioritizing the risk.
D) Developing a risk mitigation plan.
questions.answer: C) Prioritizing the risk.
questions.explanation: The lecture outlines: 'You have to find a potential risk element, then do an impact analysis and estimate the probability of occurrence and finally, you have to prioritize the risk...'

questions.question: As a project manager, what is a critical task related to communication that ensures all stakeholders, especially senior leadership, are kept informed?
options: A) Minimizing interaction with senior-level people to avoid delays.
B) Regularly communicating project progress and status.
C) Delaying decisions to allow for more thorough analysis.
D) Avoiding steering committee meetings to save time.
questions.answer: B) Regularly communicating project progress and status.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'as a project manager... one of your major task is to regularly communicate your project progress and the status to all stakeholders, specially, to the senior leadership of your client.'

questions.question: What real-world event was cited as an example of an external factor that can significantly impact ERP projects, causing delays and disruptions?
options: A) A global financial crisis
B) A major software update
C) The coronavirus (COVID) pandemic
D) A change in government regulations
questions.answer: C) The coronavirus (COVID) pandemic
questions.explanation: The lecture uses the example: 'Take for the example, this current situation of coronavirus; COVID, what has happened? So, all the projects which were running during this time, all of them got impacted.'

questions.question: When defining the organizational scope for an SAP project, why might a remote sales office in a small town be excluded?
options: A) To increase the complexity of the project.
B) Because it means additional cost, effort, and connectivity requirements.
C) To ensure all modules of SAP are implemented.
D) To prioritize technical enhancements.
questions.answer: B) Because it means additional cost, effort, and connectivity requirements.
questions.explanation: The lecture explains, 'Some of the remote, for example, sales offices may be in small towns or villages... and you may not include in your project because when you include a location it means additional cost, effort, connectivity etc.'

questions.question: Why is thorough user training considered 'very critical' in the final preparation phase, especially given the nature of an online, real-time ERP system?
options: A) To reduce the need for system performance testing.
B) Because any user mistake gets immediately reflected across the organization and impacts financial records.
C) To minimize the need for help desk support after go-live.
D) To ensure all technical enhancements are properly utilized.
questions.answer: B) Because any user mistake gets immediately reflected across the organization and impacts financial records.
questions.explanation: The lecture emphasizes, 'In the training plan, the people who are going to use system, must be trained thoroughly because it is a complex software... because it is an online system working on real times any mistake a user does, gets immediately reflected across the organization. And it is hitting your finance books.'

questions.question: For global companies or multinationals, how long can an ERP implementation project potentially take to complete across several countries?
options: A) 6 months
B) 1-2 years
C) 5 or 6 years
D) 10 years
questions.answer: C) 5 or 6 years
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'if you are talking about global companies... it can take may be 5 or 6 years to complete all the countries in the world.'

questions.question: What is a critical success factor related to decision-making in ERP projects, especially given tight project timelines?
options: A) Lengthy discussions on trivial issues.
B) Quick decision making.
C) Avoiding any decisions until the final phase.
D) Delegating all decisions to the client.
questions.answer: B) Quick decision making.
questions.explanation: The lecture advises, 'Quick decision making and avoid lengthy discussions on trivial issues. You should take quick decision because you are all bound by the project time lines which are usually very tight.'

questions.question: The lecture mentions that when implementing an ERP, 'lot of processes undergo change.' What concept is this change process referred to, and what is its underlying principle?
options: A) Technical enhancement, aiming for maximum custom code.
B) Data conversion, focusing on legacy system data.
C) Business Process Re-engineering, adapting to best practices from successful companies.
D) Organizational scope definition, limiting the number of locations.
questions.answer: C) Business Process Re-engineering, adapting to best practices from successful companies.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'something called a Business Process Re-engineering happens. So, when you implement an ERP or SAP, lot of processes undergo change because you are now capturing the best processes, which are there in the SAP product which has been you know gathered from their experience with large multinational corporations... And you need to change your business process to the best, what is happening in the successful companies.'

questions.question: Why is it important to have a support Help Desk ready from day one of Go-Live?
options: A) To manage vendor contracts.
B) To handle user problems and prevent loss of interest.
C) To conduct system performance testing.
D) To design new reports.
questions.answer: B) To handle user problems and prevent loss of interest.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'the help desk should be in place from day one and they should be ready to answer all the questions and solve their problems. Otherwise, users may lose interest and this can place the whole project in jeopardy.'

questions.question: As a project manager, what is one of the first jobs when starting a project, according to the lecture?
options: A) To begin user training.
B) To conduct a risk analysis of the project.
C) To finalize the 'To-Be' processes.
D) To implement technical enhancements.
questions.answer: B) To conduct a risk analysis of the project.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'as a project manager, one of the first job when you start a project is to do a risk analysis of the project that where things can go wrong, during the course of the project.'

questions.question: In a fixed-fee ERP project, if the project manager agrees to frequent scope changes requested by the customer, what is the likely financial consequence for the consulting company?
options: A) The project will be completed faster.
B) The consulting company will incur a loss due to increased time and cost.
C) The customer will pay more, increasing profit for the consulting company.
D) The project's quality will significantly improve without cost implications.
questions.answer: B) The consulting company will incur a loss due to increased time and cost.
questions.explanation: The lecture explains, 'Usually, these projects run on a fixed fee basis... Now, if you take more time, spend more money then that is your loss as a consultant. So, you have to keep that in mind.' And 'Avoid frequent change to requirement. So, scope change as I told earlier is a major risk.'

questions.question: What does 'Process Scope' in an ERP project primarily involve?
options: A) Deciding which hardware to use.
B) Mapping out the business processes to be covered in functional areas.
C) Determining the number of technical enhancements.
D) Selecting the project team members.
questions.answer: B) Mapping out the business processes to be covered in functional areas.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'So, one is the process scope. So, like every business, there were lot of business processes... So, we need to map out the number of processes, which are there in all the functional areas, which are being covered during that program implementation.'

questions.question: How does an 'inexperienced core team' from the client side pose a risk to an ERP project?
options: A) They will demand more technical enhancements.
B) They will have inadequate knowledge about business processes, leading to improper design inputs.
C) They will cause delays in hardware procurement.
D) They will resist user training.
questions.answer: B) They will have inadequate knowledge about business processes, leading to improper design inputs.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'Inexperienced core team, if the team from the company side, they are not experienced enough, they will have inadequate knowledge about the business processes. In that case you will not get proper design inputs. So, that is a risk parameter.'

questions.question: Why is 'Systems performance testing,' including load and performance tests, crucial before Go-Live?
options: A) To ensure all users are adequately trained.
B) To verify the accuracy of data conversion.
C) To assess how the server performs under high data volume and user load, preventing system crashes.
D) To finalize the business blueprint.
questions.answer: C) To assess how the server performs under high data volume and user load, preventing system crashes.
questions.explanation: The lecture explains, 'Systems performance testing – I was talking about the slow performance etcetera and its importance. So you have to do the load test and performance test, when everybody is working and large volume of much of data is going, how the server would be performing. Too much of data load may make it ‘hang’... they crash as the servers cannot handle so much of traffic.'

questions.question: What is a significant challenge related to 'managing change' in ERP projects, especially for employees who are not computer savvy?
options: A) Lack of technical infrastructure.
B) Resistance to learning new technology and working in a new system.
C) Difficulty in defining process scope.
D) Problems with data conversion.
questions.answer: B) Resistance to learning new technology and working in a new system.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'Managing change - Because it is a change management issue as people now have to work in a new system, they have to acquire new knowledge... So, all that can become difficult specially, if the people are elderly people and not so computer savvy... Managing this resistance to change is your challenge.'

questions.question: Which of the following components is explicitly mentioned as part of the 'Technical infrastructure scope' for an ERP project?
options: A) Payroll software
B) Business processes
C) Servers, data storage systems, and connectivity (LAN, WAN)
D) Custom reports and forms
questions.answer: C) Servers, data storage systems, and connectivity (LAN, WAN)
questions.explanation: The lecture lists, 'Technical infrastructure scope – includes the Servers, Desktops, Data storage systems, back-up devices, Disaster recovery systems, SAP and other supporting softwares, Operating Systems for the servers, connectivity like LAN, WAN etcetera.'

questions.question: Why is it crucial for a project manager to ensure all sign-offs and deliverable approvals are obtained and procedures are followed throughout the project?
options: A) To speed up the project timeline.
B) To avoid disputes and mitigate risks if people later deny agreements.
C) To reduce the need for user training.
D) To increase the number of technical enhancements.
questions.answer: B) To avoid disputes and mitigate risks if people later deny agreements.
questions.explanation: The lecture advises, 'ensure that all sign-offs and deliverable approvals are obtained and procedures are followed throughout because it is very important to get all documents signed-off. Because later on people can deny as no, I did not tell you this etc. So, there can be disputes. But, if you have a signed off document then the risk can be avoided.'

questions.question: For a large ERP implementation project, what is the minimum number of people typically involved in the team?
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'large team works for these implementations, minimum may be 15 to 20 and maximum again for this multinationals, it can go into several 100s.'

questions.question: When defining 'Functionality Scope,' why might an organization choose not to implement a specific functionality offered by the ERP software, such as payroll?
options: A) Because the ERP software does not support payroll.
B) To reduce the number of interfaces.
C) Because an existing custom-built software handles it better and can be retained.
D) To increase the need for technical enhancements.
questions.answer: C) Because an existing custom-built software handles it better and can be retained.
questions.explanation: The lecture explains, 'Some of the functionalities can be better handled by say existing softwares which have been custom built for a specific job, for example payroll... So, you want to may be retain that payroll and then, build a bridge (interface)connecting it with the SAP software.'

questions.question: What is the fundamental difference between the Business Blueprint phase and the Realization phase in an ERP project?
options: A) Blueprint focuses on user training, while Realization focuses on system testing.
B) Blueprint involves designing the 'To-Be' system, while Realization involves building the actual usable system through configuration.
C) Blueprint is for technical infrastructure setup, while Realization is for data conversion.
D) Blueprint is for risk analysis, while Realization is for Go-Live.
questions.answer: B) Blueprint involves designing the 'To-Be' system, while Realization involves building the actual usable system through configuration.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'So, in Blueprint phase you design the system and now you are building it in the Realization phase.' And for Realization: 'this is a Realization phase where you do building the actual usable system you are creating for the users (company employees).'

questions.question: Which of the following is repeatedly emphasized as a critical success factor for ERP projects?
options: A) Frequent changes to requirements.
B) Ownership and support from top management.
C) Lengthy discussions on trivial issues.
D) Inexperienced core team.
questions.answer: B) Ownership and support from top management.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'Some of the critical success factors are ownership and support from top management, again this has been said many times.'

questions.question: According to the lecture, what is a newer type of ERP project emerging, often seen when two businesses join?
options: A) Vanilla implementation
B) Standalone module implementation
C) Migration, consolidation, or harmonization
D) Custom development only
questions.answer: C) Migration, consolidation, or harmonization
questions.explanation: The lecture mentions, 'Newer types of ERP projects are emerging; migration, consolidation, harmonization etcetera. So, when two businesses join one is having one ERP, the other ERP that is a different type of project management problem altogether.'

questions.question: The lecture uses the example of public sector banks resisting computerization to illustrate what critical success factor or challenge?
options: A) The importance of technical infrastructure.
B) The challenge of managing employee resistance to change.
C) The need for extensive data conversion.
D) The benefit of quick decision-making.
questions.answer: B) The challenge of managing employee resistance to change.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'Commitment to change that is very important... So, employees must agree for a commitment to change. If they resist change, the project will not succeed. If we go back to the example of computerization of public sector banks, where the employee union had resisted computerization of banks. So, they were resisting that change.'

questions.question: What type of data, such as Material Master, Customer Master, and Vendor Master, needs to be created in the Realization phase?
options: A) Transactional data
B) Master data
C) Report data
D) Interface data
questions.answer: B) Master data
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'Also, you have to create your master data. So, all the Material Master, the Customer Master, Vendor Master; these are all thing which needs to be created on the computer...'

questions.question: Why is it important for a project manager to work closely with senior executive and delivery leaders from the client side?
options: A) To avoid making any decisions.
B) To ensure quick decision-making and prevent project delays.
C) To increase the project budget.
D) To reduce the scope of the project.
questions.answer: B) To ensure quick decision-making and prevent project delays.
questions.explanation: The lecture advises, 'work closely with the implementers senior executive and delivery leaders to discuss avenue of improvements in project execution... they are the people who are giving you decision and if they delay that decision, then your project will get delayed.'

questions.question: When reviewing risks associated with project delivery, what is a key concern mentioned that management dislikes when a project manager asks for more of it?
options: A) More time
B) More people
C) More money (cost overrun)
D) More technical enhancements
questions.answer: C) More money (cost overrun)
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'Review risks associated with project delivery - Budget overruns... if the project gets delayed there will be a cost overrun. Finally, it will cost more to the company in case of delay. Management does not like whenever a project manager will ask for more money.'

questions.question: What is the primary activity during the 'Evaluation phase' of an ERP project?
options: A) Building the actual system.
B) Doing pre-sales and understanding job complexity for quoting.
C) Training end-users.
D) Maintaining the system after Go-Live.
questions.answer: B) Doing pre-sales and understanding job complexity for quoting.
questions.explanation: The lecture describes, 'It starts with Evaluation phase, when you are actually doing the pre-sales, trying to understand the complexity of the job because you have to quote a right price, how much time it will take, how many people you will need etcetera.'

questions.question: What is a key responsibility of a project manager regarding project progress reporting?
options: A) To report progress only when requested by the client.
B) To ensure accurate project progress is reported periodically (daily or weekly).
C) To only report positive progress, hiding any issues.
D) To delegate all reporting to junior team members.
questions.answer: B) To ensure accurate project progress is reported periodically (daily or weekly).
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'Oversee and advice the periodic (daily or weekly) project leadership meetings - Ensure accurate project progress is reported. Communication is very important.'

questions.question: The lecture advises minimizing custom code development because 'the more you write codes, you can actually produce lot of bugs.' What is the direct consequence of these bugs?
options: A) Reduced project timelines.
B) Increased system performance.
C) Increased testing effort, potential errors, integration problems, and maintenance issues.
D) Simplified future upgrades.
questions.answer: C) Increased testing effort, potential errors, integration problems, and maintenance issues.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'the more you write codes, you can actually produce lot of bugs. So, you have to test it and then, there could be some errors and there could be some integration problem with the existing company product supplied and the component you have written. So, those can only give rise to a lot of maintenance issues.'

questions.question: What does ERP stand for?
options: A) Enterprise Resource Planning
B) Employee Relationship Program
C) Electronic Reporting Platform
D) Efficient Resource Provisioning
questions.answer: A) Enterprise Resource Planning
questions.explanation: The lecture explicitly mentions 'ERP or what we are talking about enterprise resource planning software.'

questions.question: What does 'Managing transition' as a challenge in ERP projects primarily refer to?
options: A) Transitioning from one project manager to another.
B) Moving over from the old system to the new system, especially with a large application portfolio.
C) Transitioning from the blueprint phase to the realization phase.
D) Transitioning from one vendor to another.
questions.answer: B) Moving over from the old system to the new system, especially with a large application portfolio.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'Managing transition is moving over from the old system to the new system and this can be a big challenge when handling large number of application portfolio.'

questions.question: Why should business requirements be 'as detailed as possible' during the Business Blueprint phase?
options: A) To allow for more custom development.
B) So that business Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) and consultants can understand the exact business needs.
C) To reduce the need for stakeholder sign-offs.
D) To accelerate the Go-Live process without further analysis.
questions.answer: B) So that business Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) and consultants can understand your exact business needs.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'Business requirements should be as detailed as possible such that the business SMEs; SMEs meaning subject matter experts and consultants can understand your exact business needs.'

questions.question: What is the final step in the five-step project risk management approach?
options: A) Prioritize the risk.
B) Do an impact analysis.
C) Have a risk mitigation plan.
D) Estimate probability of occurrence.
questions.answer: C) Have a risk mitigation plan.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'And then, you have to have a risk mitigation plan. So, for every risk, you must have a mitigation plan if this happens and how will I handle the situation that is all it means as a mitigation plan.'

questions.question: What is a challenge related to 'Technology obsolescence' in the context of ERP support and maintenance?
options: A) The difficulty in finding new employees.
B) The fact that technology gets outdated quickly in the IT industry, requiring product updates.
C) The resistance of employees to use new technology.
D) The high cost of initial ERP implementation.
questions.answer: B) The fact that technology gets outdated quickly in the IT industry, requiring product updates.
questions.explanation: The lecture mentions, 'Technology obsolescence - Technology also gets back dated; you know in IT industry it happens very often. So, products keep changing.'

questions.question: The lecture mentions that ERP projects 'usually... run on a fixed fee basis.' What implication does this have for the consulting company if the project experiences delays or increased scope without additional payment?
options: A) The consulting company will receive a bonus for extended effort.
B) The consulting company will incur a financial loss.
C) The client will be obligated to pay more for the extended duration.
D) The project will automatically be cancelled.
questions.answer: B) The consulting company will incur a financial loss.
questions.explanation: The lecture states, 'Usually, these projects run on a fixed fee basis... So, they (customer) have told you to deliver this project in one year and they will pay you so many crores and that amount is fixed. Now, if you take more time, spend more money then that is your loss as a consultant.'

questions.question: What is a key characteristic that distinguishes ERP implementation from implementing a simple sales or HR software?
options: ERP systems are less expensive.
ERP implementation is a major restructuring program impacting every process.
ERP systems only affect the finance department.
ERP systems are easier to customize.
questions.answer: ERP implementation is a major restructuring program impacting every process.
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "Major changes happen when we do an ERP implementation, because it is a major restructuring program. The business processes get change, the whole organization gets transformed... this is one software your implementing which is impacting every process of your organization."

questions.question: According to the lecture, what percentage of companies encountering barriers cited "Top management sponsorship" as a success factor?
options: 34 percent
42 percent
62 percent
82 percent
questions.answer: 82 percent
questions.explanation: The transcript mentions, "If you see the success factors - ensuring top management sponsorship; quality of communication and focusing on cultural skill and change management is 62 percent here and is pretty high. Top management sponsorship of course, is highest at 82 percent."

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three critical elements that need to integrate well for successful ERP implementation?
options: People
Process
Technology
Infrastructure
questions.answer: Infrastructure
questions.explanation: The transcript explicitly states, "People, Process and Technology need to integrate well for successful ERP implementation." Infrastructure is not mentioned as one of these three.

questions.question: What is often the first fear that comes into an employee's mind when a change or modernization happens, according to the lecture?
options: Will I be able to learn the new software?
What is in it for me?
Whether my job will remain?
Will my new skill be valued?
questions.answer: Whether my job will remain?
questions.explanation: The transcript says, "The, typical reasons people resist change is very important for you to understand. What are the major factors which people you know consider when there is a change? First one is whether my job will remain?"

questions.question: In the blueprint reference framework for change management, which of the following is NOT explicitly mentioned as part of the change management value realization track?
options: Stakeholder management and communication
Change impact analysis
Training strategy and curriculum design
Enterprise architecture framework
questions.answer: Enterprise architecture framework
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "The change management value realization if you see in the blueprint it is talking about stakeholder management and communication, change impact analysis, training strategy and curriculum design." It later mentions "enterprise architecture" as apart from this domain.

questions.question: What is identified as the major part for change management, helping people overcome fear of new technology?
options: Executive alignment
Business process improvement
Training
Value case development
questions.answer: Training
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "Training is very important as only training can help people overcome their fear of the new technology and accept the change. So, training is the major part for change management."

questions.question: Which of the following is a "People issue" identified as a major reason for the failure of large-scale transformation programs?
options: Competing resource priorities
Lack of clarity of objectives
Employee resistance
Functional boundaries
questions.answer: Employee resistance
questions.explanation: The transcript lists "People issues: - Employee resistance, Lack of middle and senior management support, Insufficient change management skills, Cynicism."

questions.question: A project manager is described as spending approximately what percentage of their time communicating?
options: 10 percent
50 percent
70 percent
90 percent
questions.answer: 90 percent
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "Communication is a very important skill requirement, I would say for a project manager. So, he actually spends almost 90 percent of his time in communicating and communicating."

questions.question: What is the primary reason given for why departments might refuse to divulge information during an ERP implementation, leading to integration issues?
options: They lack the necessary data.
They are afraid their data will be known to everybody and past mistakes exposed.
They believe the data is irrelevant to the ERP system.
They want to maintain their autonomy.
questions.answer: They are afraid their data will be known to everybody and past mistakes exposed.
questions.explanation: The transcript explains, "Many departments refuse to divulge information for example, and they do not want to give data because they are afraid that if I give my data, my data will be known to everybody I will get exposed. And then maybe we have done something wrong earlier and we had kept it suppressed. This wrong will now get exposed."

questions.question: What is the final stage in the change acceptance curve, following Awareness, Understanding, and Acceptance?
options: Implementation
Commitment
Go-Live
Evaluation
questions.answer: Commitment
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "It starts with Awareness, then it goes to Understanding, then Acceptance and finally is the Commitment."

questions.question: According to the lecture, what is the definition of "key stakeholders"?
options: All individuals or groups impacted by the change.
Those stakeholders who have the ability to impact or influence the change and are decision-makers.
Only the senior leadership of the company.
External consultants and vendors involved in the project.
questions.answer: Those stakeholders who have the ability to impact or influence the change and are decision-makers.
questions.explanation: The transcript defines key stakeholders as "Those stakeholders who have the ability to impact or influence the change the decision makers, so they are the key stakeholders."

questions.question: What is the ultimate conclusion about the nature of an ERP implementation?
options: It is primarily an IT program.
It is a business program.
It is a software upgrade.
It is a cost-cutting measure.
questions.answer: It is a business program.
questions.explanation: The transcript concludes, "ERP implementation is not an IT program, but a business program because all the time I have been talking last so many minutes is business; business; business. I never talked IT- IT -IT."

questions.question: Which of the following is a "Project management issue" that can lead to the failure of large-scale transformation programs?
options: Employee resistance
Insufficient change management skills
Initiative fatigue
Lack of clarity of objectives
questions.answer: Initiative fatigue
questions.explanation: The transcript lists "Project management issues; - Competing resource priorities... Initiative fatigue - sometimes you get a fatigue if you have to do this for a long time and it drags."

questions.question: Why is communication particularly important in software projects compared to physical projects like building a house?
options: Software projects are inherently more complex.
There is no physical progress visible in software projects, so communication is needed to show progress.
Software projects involve more stakeholders.
Physical projects do not require communication.
questions.answer: There is no physical progress visible in software projects, so communication is needed to show progress.
questions.explanation: The transcript explains, "But in a software projects what happens? You do not see anything because everything is happening in a computer and a server and physically you do not see anything. So, unless you are told or communicated, you do not see any progress and that is the problem. That is why communication is so important because nobody is seeing any development or progress taking place."

questions.question: What is the role of "Super Users" in change management?
options: To program the new ERP software.
To act as internal change drivers and ambassadors, training others.
To manage the project budget.
To make final decisions on system configuration.
questions.answer: To act as internal change drivers and ambassadors, training others.
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "Help identifying super users as internal change drivers... they can then become your ambassadors for future the internal change drivers... they actually go and finally, do that real change part i.e. give training."

questions.question: What is one of the "Communication or perception issues" that can cause ERP project failure?
options: Competing resource priorities.
Employee resistance.
Employees perceive no need for change.
Functional boundaries.
questions.answer: Employees perceive no need for change.
questions.explanation: The transcript lists "Communication or perception issues; - If employees perceive no need for change that is people do not see the value and ask as to why should we change, what good will happen?"

questions.question: The lecture emphasizes that changing a person's way of working is often more difficult than changing what?
options: Business processes
Machines
Technology
All of the above
questions.answer: All of the above
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "You can change the business process, you can change a machine, you can change a technology, no problem. Just question of money, but when you are trying to change a person’s way of working it is not money, and it can be very difficult to convince him."

questions.question: Why is it important for a project manager to involve stakeholders in decision-making and discussions, even setting deadlines for their responses?
options: To delegate responsibility.
To ensure the project stays on track and avoids delays due to indecision.
To reduce the project manager's workload.
To make stakeholders feel important.
questions.answer: To ensure the project stays on track and avoids delays due to indecision.
questions.explanation: The transcript explains, "You will need to invite them for discussions and meeting and involve them in decision making... Your response will have to be, 'sorry we do not have time because unless you give the decision my entire team gets stuck and they will not be able to do anything without your decision and we cannot move any further.'"

questions.question: What is the primary solution mentioned for addressing change management issues and helping people accept new technology?
options: Firing resistant employees.
Communication and training.
Reducing project scope.
Increasing budget.
questions.answer: Communication and training.
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "Solution is communication and training. You have to keep communicating giving them information throughout the duration of the project. At the same time, training is required because they have to actually work with the new software."

questions.question: What is the significance of the CEO's communication regarding an ERP project?
options: It is not very important as employees only listen to their direct managers.
It can give employees a different perspective and increase participation by emphasizing the project's importance for organizational survival.
It is only relevant for external stakeholders.
It primarily focuses on technical details of the implementation.
questions.answer: It can give employees a different perspective and increase participation by emphasizing the project's importance for organizational survival.
questions.explanation: The transcript says, "What sort of message has been given by the CEO is very important? He should communicate the importance of the project for the survival of the organization... when such sort of communication comes from the CEO, then employees give it a very different perspective. They realize that there must be some serious problem there which we do not understand... Then your level of participation and the quality of participation will drastically improve."

questions.question: Which of the following is a common question employees ask themselves when faced with a major change, as discussed in the lecture?
options: How much will this cost?
What is in it for me?
Who is the project manager?
When will the project end?
questions.answer: What is in it for me?
questions.explanation: The transcript mentions, "What is in it for me? Why I should change? Why I should put so much effort to learn and help implement new technology?"

questions.question: The lecture suggests that if a company wants to grow with new technology, instead of needing fewer people to do the same work, they can aim for what?
options: The same people doing less work.
The same people doing a larger amount of work.
Hiring more people to manage the technology.
Outsourcing all work.
questions.answer: The same people doing a larger amount of work.
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "But you can think it in other way and we can explain them that we can have the same people and expect that the they will be doing more work. So, instead of same work done by lesser people it could be the same people doing larger amount of work."

questions.question: What is the primary concern of project team members who are taken out of their regular roles for ERP implementation?
options: They might not get paid extra for their project work.
They fear their department will not function without them.
They worry about their role and where they will go back to after the project is over, and if their new skills will be valued.
They are concerned about the consultants' expertise.
questions.answer: They worry about their role and where they will go back to after the project is over, and if their new skills will be valued.
questions.explanation: The transcript says, "After the project is over; whether my new skill will be valued which I learned with so much effort. This is typically the concern of the project team members... So, where is my role and where do I go back to?"

questions.question: What is one of the six key focus areas for driving successful business transformation in an ERP project?
options: Reducing IT staff.
Business process improvement.
Minimizing training costs.
Avoiding organizational redesign.
questions.answer: Business process improvement.
questions.explanation: The transcript lists "Business process improvement; - It is a targeted approach to leverage ERP embedded best practices" as one of the six key focus areas.

questions.question: What does the phrase "retaining old wine in a new bottle" refer to in the context of ERP implementation?
options: Using outdated technology with new software.
Keeping existing processes intact without change after implementing an expensive ERP system.
Reusing old data in a new system.
Training old employees on new software.
questions.answer: Keeping existing processes intact without change after implementing an expensive ERP system.
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "If you are keep your existing processes intact and do not want to change then it would be like retaining old wine in a new bottle (as the saying goes), but only that now you have an expensive bottle because doing this SAP project costs lot of money."

questions.question: Which of the following is a "People issue" contributing to ERP project failure?
options: Long implementation time.
Cynicism.
Working across geographic boundaries.
Insufficient communication.
questions.answer: Cynicism.
questions.explanation: The transcript lists "People issues: - Employee resistance, Lack of middle and senior management support, Insufficient change management skills, Cynicism."

questions.question: What is "initiative fatigue" in the context of ERP project management issues?
options: Tiredness from working long hours on a single project.
A lack of interest in starting new projects.
When too many initiatives take place simultaneously, leading to exhaustion among resources.
The project manager's inability to motivate the team.
questions.answer: When too many initiatives take place simultaneously, leading to exhaustion among resources.
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "Initiative fatigue - sometimes you get a fatigue if you have to do this for a long time and it drags. When too many initiatives take place simultaneously, then something called an initiative fatigue happens amongst these resources."

questions.question: Why is "Executive alignment and governance" considered very important for ERP project success?
options: It ensures that only top executives use the new system.
It defines ownership and enables sustainable leadership action planning and accelerated decision-making.
It reduces the need for communication.
It allows for slower decision-making.
questions.answer: It defines ownership and enables sustainable leadership action planning and accelerated decision-making.
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "Executive alignment and governance; - Very important because everybody needs to be aligned and the ownership has to be defined as to who will be owning the whole program etcetera of the transformation exercise. This is very important to enable sustainable leadership action planning and accelerated decision making which is very vital for the project to be completed in time."

questions.question: What is the first step in the organizational timeline for change management implementation?
options: Training
Support and Go-Live
Mobilize and Awareness
Change Readiness
questions.answer: Mobilize and Awareness
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "It starts with 'Mobilize and Awareness' followed by the 'Change Impact', then 'Change Readiness and of course, 'Training'. That is where you try to solve the change management issue and then lastly, 'Support and Go-Live'."

questions.question: What is a key element of change management implementation that involves documenting what changes will occur in roles and organizational structure?
options: Mitigation plan for change readiness risk.
Implement organization assessments.
Document organization and role change impacts.
Roll out the communication plan.
questions.answer: Document organization and role change impacts.
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "Document organization and role change impacts; - so you have to document that. What is the organization and role changes? What are the changes going to happen? People need to know so after these, these will be changing."

questions.question: Why might employees be more accepting of information about a new ERP system from a "Super User" (colleague) rather than an external consultant?
options: Consultants are often perceived as less knowledgeable.
Colleagues are seen as more trustworthy and relatable, having experienced the change themselves.
Consultants are not allowed to give training.
Super Users have more authority.
questions.answer: Colleagues are seen as more trustworthy and relatable, having experienced the change themselves.
questions.explanation: The transcript says, "And the employees will accept more something from their own collogue rather than something from an outsider (the consultants). They may not trust the consultant because the consultant maybe telling lot of big things. But when your own colleague says no I went there I studied that I saw that and I read something and they gave me lot of information I am convinced yes that this will happen etcetera. This will be more acceptable to the employees."

questions.question: What are the two main focuses for change management in ERP transformation, as summarized in the lecture?
options: IT infrastructure and software development.
Strategic execution and the people part.
Budget control and timeline management.
Vendor selection and contract negotiation.
questions.answer: Strategic execution and the people part.
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "So, change management for ERP transformation to summarize there are two things; focus on strategic execution and focus on the people part."

questions.question: What is at the "center core" of ERP transformation, according to the summary of strategic execution and people part?
options: Cost reduction.
Value realization.
Technology adoption.
Employee satisfaction.
questions.answer: Value realization.
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "So, at the center core is value realization because end of the day you want to you know the company needs to get some value out of it through all these changes."

questions.question: What is the definition of a "stakeholder" in the context of change management?
options: Only individuals in senior management.
All individuals or groups, internal or external, who will be impacted by the change.
Only the project team members.
External vendors and suppliers.
questions.answer: All individuals or groups, internal or external, who will be impacted by the change.
questions.explanation: The transcript defines stakeholders as "All individuals or groups of individuals, internal or external who will be impacted by the change."

questions.question: Why is it important to show stakeholders demonstrations (e.g., how a new purchase order form will look) during an ERP project?
options: To get their approval for the project budget.
To engage them and keep them informed about the future design of business processes.
To test the system's functionality.
To reduce the need for training later.
questions.answer: To engage them and keep them informed about the future design of business processes.
questions.explanation: The transcript mentions, "So, we have some presentation session to show the new purchase order form will look like... This is how the senior stakeholders are engaged and kept informed about how the future design of the business processes would look and work." It also adds, "This makes them feel engaged when they see that they are been given importance."

questions.question: The lecture mentions that a security watchman doing a goods receipt transaction in SAP must be accurate because:
options: It is a legal requirement.
It is online real-time, and a mistake can impact the entire company's valuation.
He is the first person to see the delivery challan.
He needs to be computer educated.
questions.answer: It is online real-time, and a mistake can impact the entire company's valuation.
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "It is online real times and he cannot do a mistake... As this works real time thing and this mistake is impacting the entire company’s valuation. Instead of 50 pieces, he types 70 pieces."

questions.question: What is one of the "Integration issues" that can cause ERP project failure?
options: Employee resistance.
Lack of momentum.
Functional boundaries where departments refuse to share data.
Insufficient change management skills.
questions.answer: Functional boundaries where departments refuse to share data.
questions.explanation: The transcript lists "Integration issues; - integration issue in presence of functional boundaries where integrating software cuts across functional departments. So, if you have build walls or some people try to forcibly build a wall, then that is a problem... Many departments refuse to divulge information for example."

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of developing a "detailed value case" in an ERP project?
options: To justify the project's technical complexity.
To measure, track, and hold the team accountable for delivering the promised value and ROI to the customer.
To outline the project timeline.
To identify potential risks.
questions.answer: To measure, track, and hold the team accountable for delivering the promised value and ROI to the customer.
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "A detailed value case that becomes a living document and process to measure track and hold the team accountable for the delivery of value. Because you have to tell the customer about this value during your sales effort. Customer has to be told that if they invest so much money this is the value they will get. This is the return on investment and these are the benefits for the organization etcetera."

questions.question: What is the role of "Knowledge transfer and end user training" as a key focus area for successful business transformation?
options: To reduce the need for consultants.
To ensure people can successfully work in the new environment.
To document existing processes.
To manage project risks.
questions.answer: To ensure people can successfully work in the new environment.
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "Knowledge transfer and end user training - I am repeatedly saying that it is very important, for people to successfully work in this environment, that there is a proper knowledge transfer through training of the end users."

questions.question: Why is it important for management to be cautious about running multiple major programs simultaneously?
options: It can lead to initiative fatigue among resources.
It increases the overall budget.
It makes communication more difficult.
It slows down decision-making.
questions.answer: It can lead to initiative fatigue among resources.
questions.explanation: The transcript advises, "Management should be cautious that they should do only one major program at a time. Multiple small programs in parallel are fine, but complex program should be limited... When too many initiatives take place simultaneously, then something called an initiative fatigue happens amongst these resources."

questions.question: The lecture suggests that the best outcome in an ERP project comes from what?
options: Consultants making all the decisions.
Joint consultation amongst the project team and the stakeholders.
Top management dictating the changes.
Relying solely on the new technology.
questions.answer: Joint consultation amongst the project team and the stakeholders.
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "The best outcome comes from the joint consultation amongst the project team and the stakeholders. Engagement comes through involvement and of course, communication."

questions.question: What is the primary reason for the need for "Organization redesign structure and business model" during an ERP implementation?
options: To reduce employee numbers.
To get a new company structure and avoid "old wine in a new bottle" syndrome.
To simplify the IT infrastructure.
To comply with new regulations.
questions.answer: To get a new company structure and avoid "old wine in a new bottle" syndrome.
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "Organization redesign structure and business model - The organization is redesigned as, we want to get a new company structure. If you are keep your existing processes intact and do not want to change then it would be like retaining old wine in a new bottle (as the saying goes)."

questions.question: What is the purpose of a "mitigation plan for change readiness risk" in the change management timeline?
options: To identify potential risks.
To outline how to handle situations where people are not ready for change.
To assess the organizational culture.
To document organizational changes.
questions.answer: To outline how to handle situations where people are not ready for change.
questions.explanation: The transcript explains, "Mitigation plan for change readiness risk: - What is the change readiness, what are the risks involved? Then when we have this change as I said everything is a risk and for every risk you need to have a mitigation plan. Say, if this happens that people are not ready for change what is my mitigation plan? How do I handle the situation?"

questions.question: What is the core idea behind "cultural transformation" in the "people part" of ERP change management?
options: Changing the company's logo.
Changing the way the organization works.
Hiring new employees from different cultures.
Implementing new cultural events.
questions.answer: Changing the way the organization works.
questions.explanation: The transcript mentions "cultural transformation" and then explains, "Any change means it is a cultural change for the organization - the way it was working and the way it will work in future are different."

questions.question: Why is it important to "roll out the communication plan" and provide regular updates (e.g., weekly newsletters) to employees during a software project?
options: To demonstrate the project manager's communication skills.
To keep employees informed and prevent them from feeling "kept in the dark" due to lack of visible physical progress.
To gather feedback on the software's features.
To justify the project's expenses.
questions.answer: To keep employees informed and prevent them from feeling "kept in the dark" due to lack of visible physical progress.
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "So, we (employees and management) will not be kept in the dark. So, that is another fear when such software projects are implemented... So, unless you are told or communicated, you do not see any progress and that is the problem. That is why communication is so important because nobody is seeing any development or progress taking place."

questions.question: The lecture states that ERP applications contribute to the "visibility necessary to run businesses well and grow revenue and profits." What does this imply about the nature of ERP?
options: ERP systems are primarily marketing tools.
ERP systems provide integrated, real-time information across the business, enabling better decision-making.
ERP systems are only for large corporations.
ERP systems are designed to hide financial data.
questions.answer: ERP systems provide integrated, real-time information across the business, enabling better decision-making.
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "ERP applications facilitate the standardization and acceleration of business processes and contribute to the visibility necessary to run businesses well and grow revenue and profits. ERP applications form the information backbone of a business." This implies integrated, real-time information for better visibility.

questions.question: What is one of the "strategic execution" elements in the summary of ERP transformation?
options: Cultural transformation.
New skills and knowledge.
Program leadership and governance.
Stakeholder engagement.
questions.answer: Program leadership and governance.
questions.explanation: The transcript lists "Strategic part involves program strategy management, program leadership and governance and organization design."

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of identifying "impacted stakeholders" during the project preparation phase?
options: To determine who will be laid off.
To develop a plan for these people, such as new roles, retraining, or transfers.
To assign them to the project team.
To exclude them from communication.
questions.answer: To develop a plan for these people, such as new roles, retraining, or transfers.
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "So, here during the project preparation phase for example, you talk about 'identify impacted stakeholders'. So, you have to identify which are the people roles which are getting majorly impacted. And then you have to develop a plan for these people who are getting impacted. Whether we can give them new role? Retrain them in some other activities etcetera or transfer them to some other department."

questions.question: The lecture mentions that "working across geographic boundaries" can create problems for an ERP project. What is the core issue identified here?
options: Different time zones.
Lack of coordination across change initiatives.
Language barriers.
Varying legal regulations.
questions.answer: Lack of coordination across change initiatives.
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "Working across geographic boundaries; - Sometimes multinational companies are working across multiple countries... Any lack of coordination across change initiatives will creates problem for the project. So, again it is a coordination issue, because there are multiple changes initiatives happening."

questions.question: What is the main reason ERP implementation is considered a "transformational exercise" rather than just implementing software?
options: It requires a large budget.
It impacts every process and transforms the entire organization.
It involves complex technology.
It is a long-term project.
questions.answer: It impacts every process and transforms the entire organization.
questions.explanation: The transcript states, "So, it is a transformational exercise not just implementing a software. It is a special software because the entire business works across all functions on this single software. So, that is why this is not like any other simple software which you implement... But this is one software your implementing which is impacting every process of your organization."
